item.title: Ukraine’s Vulnerability Grows as Starlink Is Restricted and Russia Escalates
item.description: A huge attack cut power to 600,000 people in Kyiv, and a Pentagon-funded satellite internet program appeared to be curbed without warning.
item.dc:creator: Constant Méheut
item.media:description: Firefighters at the site of a strike at an apartment building in Kyiv on Wednesday.

item.title: What Is Starshield, SpaceX’s Military-Grade Satellite Internet Service Ukraine Relies On?
item.description: For years, Ukraine’s armed forces have relied on satellite communication services developed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX. Recent restrictions have hampered its war effort.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mac
item.media:credit: Sasha Maslov for The New York Times
item.media:description: A Starlink dish camouflaged near the Eastern frontline in the Donetsk region of Ukraine in the summer of 2023.

item.title: Burnham Pledges to Back Zelensky as Trump’s Ukraine Support Wavers
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky, who met with Britain’s prime minister, has said Ukraine received no warning of Russian attacks, but President Trump has said Washington is still “sharing intel.”
item.dc:creator: Michael D. Shear and Lara Jakes
item.media:description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcoming President Volodymyr Zelenskiy of Ukraine outside 10 Downing Street, in London, on Wednesday.

item.title: Why Easing Sanctions on Russian Diesel Is Unlikely to Lower Fuel Costs

item.title: Surging Inflation Complicates Trump’s Final Push to Sell Voters on Strong Economy

item.title: A Trump Backlash Endangers Susan Collins in the Maine Senate Race
item.description: The race in Maine, which could decide Senate control, is testing whether there is still room for Ms. Collins’s brand of moderation during a sharply polarizing presidency.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:description: Senator Susan Collins of Maine has cultivated a reputation as an independent-minded Republican who delivers for her state. As she seeks re-election, she faces a growing set of political challenges.

item.title: He’s Played It Safe. But He Could Make California History as Governor.
item.description: Xavier Becerra is a heavy favorite to become California’s first Latino governor in the modern era, though he does not talk much about the milestone.
item.dc:creator: Laurel Rosenhall, Jennifer Medina and Orlando Mayorquín
item.media:description: Xavier Becerra attending a “No on Prop 39" event, in opposition to a voter identification ballot initiative, in Los Angeles this month.

item.title: A New World of Lung Cancer Therapy Awaits Pope Leo
item.description: Lung cancer is still a leading cause of cancer death, but that rate is half what it was in the 1990s, partly because newly developed treatments are working.
item.dc:creator: Gina Kolata and Carolyn Y. Johnson
item.media:description: Pope Leo greeted his personal physician, Luigi Carbone, as he arrived at the Gemelli Hospital in Rome on Tuesday to remove a lung nodule.

item.title: Pope Leo’s Cancer Diagnosis: What Happens Next
item.description: Pope Leo XIV was diagnosed with a common form of lung cancer. The Vatican said that he was walking and receiving therapy after an operation to remove a cancerous nodule.
item.dc:creator: Laura Chung
item.media:description: Pope Leo arriving at a hospital in Rome on Tuesday.
